evidence.note: CONFIRMED: ddflow complete has no --check flag (argparse errors with 'unrecognized arguments: --check', exit 2). Regression test tests/test_complete_check.py fails on the unfixed code (exit 2 vs expected 0/1) and the fix adds a read-only --check; it passes on the fixed code (3 passed).

git commit 5ee97566d adds --check to complete: _check_report in finish.py, the check Param in declared/lifecycle/outcome.py, check branches in lifecycle_cli.py render; tests/test_complete_check.py; golden snapshots regenerated.

chunk_findings.detail: `_check_report` decides `may_complete` and the returned `blockers` only from `v.blockers`, while the caller passes `hard` separately and `hard` can contain blockers that are not in `v.blockers`. For example, `CM._own_branch_unmerged(...)` is added to `hard` but does not mutate `v.blockers`. If an item has no ordinary blockers but its own branch is unmerged, `complete(..., check=True)` reaches `_check_report` with `v.blockers=[]` and `hard=["own branch ... unmerged"]`; the function returns `O.ok("item.checked", may_complete=True, blockers=[])` (exit 0). A real completion would refuse on the hard blocker, so the dry-run falsely reports that nothing is unmet. The same omission means hard blockers are absent from the `check_only` data even when other blockers make `may_complete` false. `hard` should be included in the blockers/may_complete calculation or returned as its own required field.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/lifecycle/complete/finish.py:_check_report

chunk_findings.detail: For `--check`, the text branch distinguishes only between empty `blockers` and non-empty `blockers`; it never distinguishes the specified “could not run” case. The missing-item test runs `ddflow complete NOPE --check` and expects exit code 2, but if the check returns no blockers (the natural result when there is no item to evaluate), this code returns `NOPE may complete (0 unmet conditions).` even though the check failed to run. If instead a could-not-run error is placed in `blockers`, the same code prints it as “unmet condition(s),” which is also wrong because exit 2 means the check could not run, not that completion conditions are unmet.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/declared/lifecycle_cli.py:complete_text

chunk_findings.detail: The test claims to verify that `--check` “writes nothing,” but it only asserts that the item state is not `done`. A check implementation that writes a policy grant, approval request, or other completion-related event while leaving the item open would pass this test. That is exactly the class of bug this change is meant to prevent: the original incident involved a standing policy grant being recorded before the operator saw the request. The test should compare the event log/state before and after the check, not merely the final item state.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_complete_check.py:test_complete_check_reports_unmet_conditions_and_writes_nothing

chunk_findings.detail: `test_complete_check_exits_zero_when_nothing_is_unmet_and_does_not_complete` calls `run_cli` with an unknown `--model` parameter (`--model`, `"claude-opus-5"`), which will cause `run_cli` or the underlying CLI argument parser to reject the argument with a parser error or exit code 2 rather than exercising the successful completion check path.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_complete_check.py:40

chunk_findings.detail: `_check_report` decides the dry-run verdict from `v.blockers` only and ignores the `hard` list it receives. In the normal path, `CM._own_branch_unmerged(st, cfg, it, repo)` is added to `hard`, but it is not added to `v.blockers`; therefore, for an item whose soft blockers are empty but whose own branch is unmerged, `_check_report` sees `blockers == []`, sets `may_complete=True`, and returns `O.ok("item.checked", ...)` before reaching the `if hard:` branch. In that scenario `ddflow complete --check` exits 0 and reports no unmet conditions even though a real completion would be refused by a hard, non-forceable blocker. Even when `v.blockers` is non-empty, the machine-readable `blockers`/`may_complete` data omit the hard blockers, so the caller is told what remains without being told about conditions that cannot be overridden.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/lifecycle/complete/finish.py:_check_report

chunk_findings.detail: The new `--check` output path is built solely from `blockers`; it has no handling for the declared `exit 2 = could not run` case and ignores any `note`/approval/policy explanation. For the missing-item scenario exercised by `test_complete_check_could_not_run_on_a_missing_item`, if the check result signals failure by exit code 2 but does not populate `blockers` (or puts the reason in `note`), the CLI prints `NOPE may complete (0 unmet conditions).` That tells the operator a nonexistent item may complete, contradicting the stated contract and the dry-run purpose. The new test only asserts the exit code, so this wrong text can pass.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/declared/lifecycle_cli.py:complete_text

chunk_findings.detail: The test name and docstring claim the check “writes nothing,” but the only assertion is that the item state is not `done`. If `--check` still evaluates policy and files an approval request or records a policy grant while leaving the item open, this test passes. Given the original failure mode (a standing policy granting `complete.force`), a read-only check that writes an approval-request event but does not complete would satisfy every assertion here, so the regression test does not actually prove the required read-only behavior.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_complete_check.py:test_complete_check_reports_unmet_conditions_and_writes_nothing

chunk_findings.detail: The delta changes `_check_report` so a hard-only unmet item now returns a failed outcome with `may_complete=False`, `blockers=[]`, and `hard=["own branch ... unmerged"]`, but it does not change the text `--check` branch previously reported to decide success/exit from the `blockers` list alone. Given an item whose only unmet condition is an unmerged own branch, the CLI text layer still sees an empty `blockers` list and takes the success path, printing `... may complete (0 unmet conditions)` and exiting 0 even though the new check outcome says completion is not allowed and a real completion would refuse. The same blocker-only text branch also still has no distinct representation for the required exit-2 “could not run” case. The fix must either merge hard-only blockers into the caller-visible blocker list or update the text layer to use `may_complete`/`hard` and a distinct failure code.

chunk_findings.detail: This test asserts only that the exit code is 2. On the unfixed code, `--check` is not a recognized option, so `ddflow complete NOPE --check` fails during argument parsing and argparse exits with 2. Therefore this test passes before the feature exists and does not demonstrate the intended “could not run” dry-run path; it also would pass if a future regression caused `--check` to be rejected as an unknown option. The test should assert that the output comes from the check path (for example, mentions the missing item or a could-not-run check) so it fails on the unfixed code.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_complete_check.py:test_complete_check_could_not_run_on_a_missing_item

chunk_findings.detail: When `hard` is non-empty but `v.blockers` also contains soft, force/approval-liftable conditions, `_check_report` prints all listed conditions and then unconditionally appends “None of these is lifted by `--force` or an approval”. For example, an item with `hard=["own branch unmerged"]` and `v.blockers=["unavailable required gate"]` will produce a report that lists both conditions and says neither can be lifted, even though the unavailable-gate blocker is exactly the kind of condition the standing `complete_unavailable` policy/approval path can grant. The code suppresses the `_only_unavailable` explanation because the `if hard:` branch is taken first, so the dry-run misstates the approvals/policy that are needed for the soft conditions, contrary to the intended read-only behavior.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/lifecycle/complete/finish.py:_check_report

chunk_findings.detail:
The `--check` branch renders only `blockers` and drops the `note`/approval/policy explanation that the non-check path prints. For a normal shown check result such as `data = {"check_only": True, "blockers": ["tests not passing"], "note": "policy rule complete.force would grant this completion"}`, the CLI prints only `1 unmet condition(s) for T1:
  - tests not passing` and never says that a policy would grant the completion, despite the new `check` parameter’s help promising to print “approvals needed” and “what policy would grant.” The earlier refutation only showed that a missing item exits before this text path; it does not address shown check results that carry a note/policy explanation.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/declared/lifecycle_cli.py:complete_text
